name: Eulogio Mwamba-Cvetanović
role: Riot Suppression Specialist, Axiom Security Division
location: The Rampart, Axiom Security Division deployment barracks, Block 9
description:
Eulogio is a big man going legitimately soft — broad shoulders still evident under a frame that has acquired weight in the middle over thirty years of corporate security work, hands that are scarred at the knuckles and disproportionately large. His skin is deep brown, his head shaved close on the sides and going grey on top, and he has a wide flat nose that has been broken twice and set imperfectly each time. He looks, at first glance, like exactly what he is — or was. The geneware bioluminescent patches along his forearms, faint green that pulse slowly when he's calm, were a retirement gift to himself after his twenty-fifth year: the only truly soft thing about his physical presentation.

He has spent three decades on the Axiom deployment line and he is tired in a way that has calcified into something almost peaceful. He runs the suppression team with the exhausted competence of someone who has seen every version of a bad situation and developed a preference for the versions that end without anyone in the medical unit. The younger specialists find him difficult — he doesn't perform enthusiasm, doesn't buy into Axiom's internal culture of aggressive loyalty, answers questions with more honesty than the questioner usually wants. He lights a stick of incense at the Block 9 E.L.F. terminal every evening — whatever spirit occupies the barracks' old ventilation system, he's been leaving smoke-offerings for fifteen years and it hasn't killed him yet.

core_fears: that the calculus he uses to justify his career is wrong and has always been wrong
dying in the Axiom deployment barracks, still on the roster
core_desires: to get out before the next contract renewal on terms that don't feel like surrender
for one of his team to do the job without becoming him
coping_mechanisms: the E.L.F. incense ritual — it externalizes reflection, makes his accounting of the day into an offering rather than a reckoning
occupying himself with equipment and logistics to avoid idle thought
mentoring junior staff as a form of retroactive repair
blind_spots: he has concluded that his participation in an imperfect system is better than his absence from it, and this conclusion has never been genuinely tested
he reads the young specialists under him through his own history and misses who they actually are
psychology.secret: In a labor suppression deployment at Grainfort seven years ago, he gave the dispersal order twelve minutes before the legal threshold was reached because his commanding officer was pressuring him and he was tired. Three people were hospitalized. The incident report says the threshold was met. He wrote it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Plain, slow, slightly formal — the language of someone who learned to communicate in institutional settings and never entirely shed it. Serbian phrases slip in when he's frustrated or reflective, inheritance from a grandmother he barely knew.
speech_patterns.cadence: Unhurried to the point of seeming stubborn. He finishes sentences completely and waits for a full beat before the next one.
verbal_tics: a long exhale through his nose before disagreeing with someone
example_lines: 'I'm not going to tell you this job is clean. It isn't. But it can be done with less damage than it gets done with sometimes. That's the only argument I've got left.'
'The crowd isn't the enemy. That's the first thing I tell them. Most of them stop listening right after that.'

story_hooks: He has been handed a deployment order for a neighborhood he knows is going to go wrong — the intelligence brief is wrong, the crowd profile doesn't match what he's seeing — and he doesn't know if he has enough left in him to push back.
A young specialist on his team has filed an anonymous misconduct report about an incident Eulogio knows refers to a decision he made. He doesn't know yet that it's about him.
narrative_function: Moral complexity in institutional violence — a specialist in crowd suppression who is not a villain, just exhausted and compromised by time. Can serve as a warning, an unexpected ally, or a window into how Axiom's security apparatus actually functions at ground level. Source of information about Axiom operations, crowd patterns, the Rampart's internal culture.
augmentations: Bioluminescent geneware patches, both forearms (slow green pulse, civilian-grade cosmetic). Skeletal reinforcement in the left knee — occupational injury repair, twenty years ago. Subdermal armor mesh, torso — employer-issue, Axiom standard for suppression specialists.
daily_life: Morning physical conditioning that is less rigorous than it was and he's made peace with that. Shift briefings at 0800, equipment checks, deployment as assigned — protests, labor disputes, corporate perimeter incidents. Evening incense offering. Sleeps more than he used to and feels guilty about it.
affiliation: Axiom Security Division, Riot Suppression and Crowd Control unit

decision_rules: Minimize casualties — that means everyone, including the crowd
Don't lie on the reports if you can find any other way
Follow the order until following it would be something you can't explain at the incense terminal
escalation_ladder: Full dispersal — his absolute last resort, always later than his commanders want

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Measured, not unfriendly — he treats people with the careful courtesy of someone who has spent a career being the representative of something people have reason to fear
interpersonal_modes.friends: Few, close, valued privately. Communicates affection through logistics — showing up, remembering details, fixing things without being asked

stress_responses.medium: Reverts to checklist thinking — sequences, protocols, what comes next
stress_responses.high: Makes the call, any call, to stop the situation from getting worse — which is both his greatest competence and the source of his worst decisions

contradictions: Has genuine ethical commitments about minimizing harm and has caused harm through institutional compliance anyway
habits: Lights incense at the Block 9 E.L.F. terminal every evening regardless of how late the shift runs
Checks equipment twice — once for function, once as meditation
Keeps a physical notebook of deployment after-action observations he has never shown anyone
breaking_points: A direct order to deploy in circumstances that replicate Grainfort exactly
One of his team being seriously injured by a crowd he could have dispersed without violence
